prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with knee injury after a side impact at intersection. The patient had 17 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1090; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Some exam findings support the injury; other tests are normal.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- The same service was billed twice for the same date, and the provider admitted the second charge was a repeat.
text: Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection, reporting pain and swelling in the right knee. The mechanism of injury and the force involved are consistent with the knee complaints described. Over the course of 17 visits, the patient received conservative management including physical therapy, range-of-motion exercises, and anti-inflammatory medication. Treatment followed a typical progression, with visit frequency decreasing as symptoms improved and function returned. Examination revealed some findings that support the presence of a soft-tissue injury, including localized tenderness and limited flexion, while other orthopedic and neurovascular tests were within normal limits. No prior injury or treatment to the same body region is known. Billing records show the same service was entered twice for one date of service; the provider has acknowledged that the second entry was a duplicate and should not have been charged.
